public_rationale: The claim itself says MSN still gets nearly two billion viewers a month. So the contract reads 'destroyed' as ruined editorial quality, not lost traffic. The Guardian reported on May 30, 2020 that Microsoft had decided to 'stop employing humans to select, edit and curate news articles' on its homepages (e1). In November 2023, people familiar with the site told CNN that Microsoft's growing reliance on automation and AI over human editors 'appears to be behind' MSN's amplification of false and bizarre stories (e2, quoted by Slashdot). Futurism, quoted in the same Slashdot post, said MSN published bogus Bigfoot and mermaid stories 'in the wake of ditching its human editors in favor of automation' (e3). In September 2023, Windows Central reported on an obituary of Brandon Hunter that was distributed via MSN (e4). It said the obituary made 'multiple egregious errors' and 'appeared to be heavily plagiarized' from TMZ Sports. A third-party site, Race Track, published that obituary. The cited reporting does not show that Microsoft's own AI wrote these stories. Windows Central also notes that Microsoft blamed a human for a separate travel-guide error (e4).
limitations: CNN's findings are cited through Slashdot's quotation because the CNN page could not be read.
The link between automation and the false stories rests on unnamed people familiar with the site and on former editors. Microsoft did not confirm it.
The Futurism original was not read directly. Its Bigfoot finding is cited through Slashdot.
MSN traffic was not checked, so the evidence does not test a traffic-based reading of 'destroyed'.

The reporting does not show who or what wrote the Bigfoot stories. It does not show that Microsoft's own AI wrote any of the cited stories. A strict reading of 'an artificial intelligence that posts made up stories' could therefore be disputed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft destroyed MSN.com by replacing human staff with AI that posts fabricated and wrong stories.

statement.excerpt: Microsoft destroyed MSN.com — a page that gets nearly two billion viewers a month — by replacing its human staff with an artificial intelligence that posts made up stories about bigfoot and stealing other outlets' stories and still getting the details wrong.

from_speaker: "a page that gets nearly two billion viewers a month"
"by replacing its human staff with an artificial intelligence"
"stealing other outlets' stories and still getting the details wrong"
our_interpretation: He says MSN still 'gets nearly two billion viewers a month', so 'destroyed' is not read as a traffic collapse. It is read as ruining MSN's editorial quality and credibility.

The claim holds if (a) Microsoft replaced MSN's human editors with automated or AI curation, (b) MSN then published fabricated stories (for example Bigfoot) and garbled, copied stories with errors, and (c) credible reporting ties (b) to (a).
'An artificial intelligence that posts' is read as the automated curation system that picks and publishes stories. It does not require Microsoft's AI to have written each story.
The traffic figure ('nearly two billion') is an aside and is not scored.
criteria.support_condition: Reporting showing Microsoft replaced MSN's human curators with automation or AI, that MSN then ran fabricated and error-ridden copied stories, and that people familiar with the site attribute this to the automation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that human editors remained in control, that the false stories were not linked to automation, or that MSN's content quality did not decline after the change.

evidence.excerpt: Around 27 individuals employed by PA Media – formerly the Press Association – were told on Thursday that they would lose their jobs in a month’s time after Microsoft decided to stop employing humans to select, edit and curate news articles on its homepages.
evidence.explanation: Confirms the first link in the chain: Microsoft replaced the human staff who curated MSN with automated systems.

evidence.excerpt: Microsoft's decision to increasingly rely on the use of automation and artificial intelligence over human editors to curate its homepage appears to be behind the site's recent amplification of false and bizarre stories, people familiar with how the site works told CNN.
evidence.explanation: CNN's sources tie MSN's false and bizarre stories to the switch from human editors to automation and AI. This supports the causal link.

evidence.excerpt: MSN "has also published other junk content, including bogus stories about fishermen catching mermaids and Bigfoot spottings," reports the tech news site Futurism, "in the wake of ditching its human editors in favor of automation.
evidence.explanation: Confirms that MSN published bogus Bigfoot stories after replacing editors with automation, matching his 'made up stories about bigfoot'.

evidence.excerpt: Along with being error-laden, the article on Race Track appeared to be heavily plagiarized from an obituary published by TMZ Sports.
evidence.locator: paragraph beginning 'The post on Race Track'
evidence.explanation: MSN distributed a copied obituary that got the details wrong. This matches 'stealing other outlets' stories and still getting the details wrong', although the story was written by a partner site, not by Microsoft's own AI.
